scores.rationale: Multiple snippets, especially from LoreMarq2010, explicitly state the stylized fact (SF8) that chlorophyll concentration decreases with irradiance and use it to constrain model structure (snippets 3, 4, 8, 13). Kooy2010 (5) and Zonn98b (10) corroborate that relative chlorophyll is high at low irradiance, consistent with the fact. The main tension comes from Zonneveld (6, 14), which note that while chlorophyll production rate decreases with decreasing irradiance, the chlorophyll cell quota still increases at low light due to reduced dilution by growth—an alternative mechanistic framing that nonetheless ends up consistent with higher chlorophyll at low irradiance (i.e., decreasing with irradiance). These were labeled 'contradicts' because they challenge the simplistic production-based interpretation, but directionally they align. Overall the corpus provides strong, repeated support for the fact with little genuine conflict.

Snippet 5 weakly contradicts by showing light-stored cabbage retained more chlorophyll than dark-stored, though this concerns storage chlorophyll loss rather than photoacclimation, so its bearing is ambiguous. The remaining snippets are off-topic, concerning photoperiod/salinity (no effect), temperature, senescence, biosynthesis genetics, or fish reproduction. Overall the corpus clearly corroborates the stylized fact with little genuine conflict, though much of the support comes from a single source family.
